The roof audit resolves the earlier three IDs against current edges and requires three connected eave/opening/eave segments.

The displayed current fresh dormer producer has no TransverseGable outputs and the other CrossGable links begin empty; an actually supported route supplying two cuts was not established. findings_and_questions.kind: conditional sampled-flow consistency question, fresh-route reachability not shown
findings_and_questions.first_contract: The three split edges share endpoints and retain the old face references. The ray kernel admits edge parameters from -0.002 through 1.002, so a common-grid sample whose downhill ray lands at or close to a shared endpoint can be accepted by two edge receivers. Both primary and supplemental producers retain sampled points separately, while the audit compares the total sample count to the single expected grid and requires coverage.
findings_and_questions.condition: Both same-face receivers must create retained networks, the shared ray must satisfy the height and intersection checks for both, and any later mutation/cleanup must leave both samples. A duplicate with full coverage increases the count beyond expectation; missing coverage also fails the separate coverage predicate. A supported current fresh-route split case was not established, and no geometry was generated.
findings_and_questions.future_direction: Define boundary ownership for shared receiver segments or deduplicate per-face sample assignment without losing eave/apron physical identity; preserve tolerances, meaningful empty/partial modes and intended audit coverage.
relationships: The original /root/lens12_frontier 059 read noted existing_edges is captured once per link and requested actual receiver and caller proof; this question concerns overlapping ray acceptance on distinct shared-endpoint receivers, not necessarily duplicate edge IDs. Related RAW-SOURCE-002 is broader raw sampling inventory rather than an automatic alias.

findings_and_questions.first_contract: The first parent-recipient pass filters weather containment and obstacles, chooses the candidate closest to desired plan, and only then tests whether its face is at least 0.08 m below the source. If the selected candidate is too high, it does not try another candidate in that pass; the subsequent fallback starts at nonzero distances and does not retry the zero-offset target.
findings_and_questions.condition: A higher eligible face must win selection over a lower eligible face at the same zero-offset point, the lower target must be physically valid, and no usable nonzero fallback may be found. Actual supported overlapping face geometry, terrain/obstacle policy, and final drainage acceptance are unproven. The consequence is a possible change to another outlet disposition, not a demonstrated runtime failure.
findings_and_questions.future_direction: Determine allowed parent-face overlap and intended obstacle/downhill priority. If all qualifying lower faces must be considered, apply the elevation predicate before choosing the nearest candidate and preserve fallback and collision semantics deliberately.
relationships: Related context is original /root/segovb 059 READ-L11-420 parent-face obstacle-aware versus fallback notes and Q2262 ground-candidate fallback acceptance, but the zero-offset candidate-selection predicate is a different first operation; no automatic alias.

findings_and_questions.kind: open numerical and ownership policy question
findings_and_questions.first_contract: Weather containment applies a general odd-even polygon test to the outer outline and excludes cutouts with the same predicate. The predicate uses strict crossing comparisons, so boundary membership can depend on which polygon side is queried; drainage sampling separately uses a convex sign/tolerance predicate.
findings_and_questions.condition: The intended treatment of exact outer and hole boundary contacts and admissible convex/concave face shapes is not established. The two kernels have distinct roles; difference alone does not prove a defect.
findings_and_questions.future_direction: Specify boundary and polygon-shape semantics at the owner of weather-recipient admission and compare actual downstream fall-cone and sampling requirements before unifying kernels.
relationships: 059 /root/lens12_frontier explicitly cautioned against aliasing weather projection and convex sampling by a common normalization remedy. 774 RAW-SOURCE-002 retains signed zero, convexity, holes and numerical ordering as independent constraints.
